answer.generated: The two primary design issues for distributed systems engineering are transparency and openness. Transparency concerns whether a distributed system should appear to users as a single entity or if they need to understand its distributed nature. Openness involves designing systems with standard protocols to promote interoperability versus using specialized protocols that limit flexibility. These issues arise because distributed systems require balancing ease of use against technical complexity.
